### Remove transport type-9 fragmentation

Glenn ruled remove (audit 13). Branch rowan/remove-type9-fragmentation at 0689412d: unreachability confirmed; the code, config field, status code, 41 counters, standard sections and the model's fragment half are gone; server required_memory at 1000 clients drops 379 MB and the client's from 29.3 MB to 20.3 MB. Owed: a full fleet run at the head; five one-line negative controls; timing the split lock-in sweep under the sanitizers; a Windows light-profile ceiling measurement; the fragment text left in proofs/tla/Link.tla (editing it pushes MCRNChannel past the 110 s TLC budget). Rebase onto main (conflicts with the counter renumbering).

From: Audit item 13; Glenn, 2026-10-31

### Seed the message resend delay from the measured RTT

The two channels nightly seeds that fail every run (4879047, 4879943) time out because the message layer waits its 2000 ms default while the transport has already measured RTT. Branch rowan/resend-seeded-rtt at 511ead80: works on macOS, TLC and standard m9.2 updated. Owed: diagnose the Linux test_light_profile_server_1000_required_memory failure; the full nightly seed range; re-measure the ordered stream's completion multiple; squash the WIP commits.

From: Red channels nightly

### macOS network thread just above default priority

Since #624 the macOS network thread runs at SCHED_RR maximum and outranks the game thread. Branch rowan/macos-net-thread-priority at 1e9ecedf (priority 32): msgx P=32 p99 43.3 to 19.6 us on mini-m5. Owed: 200+ single-cell closed_port runs and a contention A/B against 47 to show #624's fix holds. If it does not hold under contention, Glenn decides between network latency and game-thread p99.

## Audit items not yet fixed

Suspects from FABLE-AUDIT.md that nothing on main fixes. Each is verified at the cited line first; a confirmed defect gets a lock-in test and a negative control.

### Keep-alive slot count compared unsigned

rocketnet_client_validate_keep_alive casts the u32 slot count to int, so 2^31 or more is refused, against the ruling that the client accepts any count with index below it. Unit cases at 2^31 and UINT32_MAX, and a negative control.

From: #730 follow-on

### A create test that fails on second_public_address alone

The whole-config create test goes red under the old truncation only because loopback_hub is also cut off.

From: #737 follow-on

### Drain limitation text after #740

docs/CLIENT-IO.md and TRANSPORT-INTERNALS.md 'current staging and drain limitations' still describe the drain bound #740 fixed.

From: #740 follow-on

### ROCKETNET_MAX_CHANNELS CMake option

Pass it through as ROCKETNET_MAX_CLIENTS is, document it, and give it a CI build.

From: Audit item 171 follow-on

### Portable sendmmsg keeps the unsent rest of a batch

On a full socket the portable sendmmsg path drops the rest of the batch; GSO now keeps it (audit 111). Same rule: spread across updates, never drop.

From: Audit item 111 follow-on

### Two-phase io_uring send staging

When more than 10240 completions arrive ahead of its sends, the io_uring send index still ratchets and outbound runs about one update in three under a flood. Give send staging commit and complete phases as RIO has.

From: #738 follow-on

### A duplicated deferred packet does not redeliver its code-0 prefix

Audit 101 remainder, MESSAGES.md m1.4 rule 2. Recommended: remember the deferred packet and how many records were processed, so a duplicate skips them.

From: Audit item 101

### Windows iocp and rio re-flush

Audit 88 and 124: measure on captain, then add re-flush counters if the measurement supports it.

From: Audit items 88, 124

### Server-stop functional case asserts no send failures

The Windows cut-off of a flushed bank at stop was never reproduced on captain. Asserting the send-failure counter does not move during stop gives the check a way to fail; it needs a small test accessor for a stopped server's transport stats.

From: Stop-spread follow-on

The page's exact byte figures go stale with every merge. Generate them, with a CI check that the page matches the generator.

docs/RELEASING.md asks for it; nothing enforces it. Extend tools/check_release_tsan.py to require nightly-ci.yml, msan and CBMC green at the tagged commit.

## Decisions for Glenn

Choices that change behavior, remove machinery, or touch repository and fleet settings.

### Cap the single-packet resend delay at timeout/4

Audit 16: with message_resend_delay_max_ms above reliable_message_timeout_ms/4, a single-packet record gets fewer than four sends before timeout. Recommended: cap it as chunks are. Then both resend classes share one delay, and the two resend queues could collapse to one; that removes machinery.

From: Audit item 16

### Wire version after removing type 9

The removal leaves ROCKETNET_WIRE_VERSION unchanged because no surviving packet changes a byte.

From: Audit item 13

### Unit tests and the process environment

Unit cases still reach the environment through the public creates, safe only because the runner clears every name the SDK reads. Stricter: route about 320 creates through the injected-environment variants. Recommended: keep the runner boundary. Also move the XDP gateway address read from socket open to create.

From: #794

### Branch protection on main

No ruleset requires any check on main (audit 44).

From: Audit item 44

### A runner label for the nightly frame budget held only by amd-2 and amd-3

rocketnet-quiet also covers hetzner2; the frame budget is a wall-clock gate that compares only on one machine class.

From: #731
